evidence.quote: We also do not con- sider Li2, the second candidate of Li et al. (2015), because there are two radial velocity measurements in the literature which disagree: LAMOST reports −60 ± 10 km s−1 whilst SDSS reports -160.8 ± 3.4 km s−1. The simplest explanation is that this star is an unresolved binary and thus the reported radial velocities are not representative of the true systemic velocity.

notes: T:p4-b6: Table 1 reports 41 candidates with P_bound < 0.5, but its HVS Survey row names only HVS1, HVS4-10 and HVS12-24 plus unspecified 'others'; the 'others' lack individual identifiers and are omitted. HVS2/US708 and HVS3/HE 0437-5439 are grouped aliases, and LAMOST-HVS1-3 is expanded to three stars. T:p1-b9 and T:p6-b3: Li10 is LAMOST J115209.12+120258.0 and is retained as the sole late-type unbound candidate. T:p4-b11: SDSSJ124043.01+671034.68 is a prior white-dwarf hypervelocity candidate now reported bound, hence follow_up. T:p2-b9: Li2 is a prior Li et al. (2015) candidate excluded because of discrepant radial velocities; it is recorded as follow_up without a boundness conclusion. T:p2-b9: J004330.06+405258.4 is an M31 hypervelocity star, not a Galactic-unbound candidate, and is omitted. T:p2-b7: HD 5223 is only a prior-literature example and lacks a current-paper boundness assessment, so it is omitted. Retained Table 1 entries are candidates_found; historical candidates explicitly ruled out or excluded are follow_up.

HVS1: No equatorial coordinates, parallax, proper motions, galactocentric radius, total Galactic rest-frame speed, or exact bound probability are reported for HVS1. Table 1 lists HVS1 among candidates with P_bound < 0.5 (T:p4-b6; see also T:p4-b3), but this is a selection threshold rather than an individual numerical result, so it is not recorded as a per-star bound probability.

HVS4: HVS4 appears only in Table 1 (T:p4-b6) as part of the grouped entry "HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others" attributed to the Hypervelocity Star Survey (32 stars; Brown et al. 2005, 2007, 2014). This is a survey-level grouping, not an individual result for HVS4, and the supplied material reports no individual astrometric, kinematic, distance, or bound-probability values for HVS4. No quantities can therefore be extracted for this target.

HVS5: HVS5 is not discussed individually in the supplied text. It is only covered generically by Table 1's statement that the Hypervelocity Star Survey discovered 32 of the 41 candidates with P_bound < 0.5, including "HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others" (T:p4-b6). The paper does not report star-specific coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HVS5 itself, so no individual quantities can be extracted.

HVS6: HVS6 is not individually discussed or tabulated with measured quantities. It is only included within the Hypervelocity Star Survey group listing in Table 1 at T:p4-b6 ("HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others"), which gives no individual values for HVS6.

HVS7: HVS7 is not individually discussed or tabulated with measurements. It is included only within the Hypervelocity Star Survey entry in Table 1 as part of “HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others” (T:p4-b6 / I:p4-b6). That table selects candidates with P_bound < 0.5, but this is a sample-selection threshold rather than an individual reported value; no individual quantities for HVS7 are supplied.

HVS8: HVS8 is identified in the supplied paper only via Table 1 (T:p4-b6 / I:p4-b6), where the "Hypervelocity Star Survey" row lists "HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others" (32 stars) as candidates with P_bound < 0.5. No individual astrometric, photometric, distance, radial-velocity, Galactocentric velocity, galactocentric radius, or bound-probability value is reported for HVS8 anywhere in the text, figures, or tables; the paper says individual measurements are collected in the external Open Fast Stars Catalog, which is not provided here. The P_bound < 0.5 membership is a selection threshold for Table 1 rather than an individual reported result, so no per-star quantity is extracted.

HVS9: The target star HVS9 is only mentioned as part of a group listing in Table 1 ("HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others" under the Hypervelocity Star Survey, T:p4-b6). The paper does not report any individual values (coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motions, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound probability) specifically for HVS9. Per the scientific rules, group values and selection thresholds are not individual results, so no quantities can be assigned to this star.

HVS10: HVS10 appears only as part of the aggregated listing "HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others" (32 stars) attributed to the Hypervelocity Star Survey in Table 1 (T:p4-b6), which gives no individual values for HVS10. The paper reports no position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability specific to HVS10; the detailed discussion concerns Li10 (LAMOST J115209.12+120258.0), GD 492, and HVS1/HVS3. No quantities meeting the extraction rules are therefore available for the target star.

HVS12: HVS12 is only identified in Table 1 at T:p4-b6 as part of the Hypervelocity Star Survey group (“HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others”) among candidates with P_bound < 0.5. No star-specific position, distance, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactic rest-frame velocity, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability is reported in the supplied material; the table entry is a selection/group statistic, not an individual value.

HVS13: HVS13 is not individually discussed in the supplied text. It appears only in the grouped Table 1 entry "HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others" (T:p4-b6; I:p4-b6), whose caption states that the table lists hypervelocity candidates with P_bound < 0.5. No star-specific numerical values, uncertainties, or coordinates for HVS13 are reported. The P_bound < 0.5 mention is a sample selection threshold rather than an individual result, so no quantities are extracted.

HVS14: The target star HVS14 is not discussed individually anywhere in the supplied text, tables, or figures. It appears only implicitly within the "HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others" entry for the Hypervelocity Star Survey in Table 1 (LOCATION T:p4-b6 / I:p4-b6), which is a group listing of stars with P_bound < 0.5. That entry is a sample/selection description rather than an individual reported measurement, so no quantities (position, distance, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, rest-frame speed, bound probability) are reported specifically for HVS14. Per the rules, selection thresholds and sample statistics are not individual results, so the quantities array is empty.

HVS15: The target star HVS15 is not individually discussed or tabulated with measurements in the supplied material. Table 1 (T:p4-b6) lists it only as part of the Hypervelocity Star Survey grouping: "HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others" (32 stars). No individual coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motions, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HVS15 is reported. Group counts in Table 1 and the text (e.g., T:p4-b3, T:p2-b9) are sample statistics and do not constitute individual results.

HVS16: The target star HVS16 is never discussed individually in the supplied material. It appears only implicitly within the collective entry "HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others" of Table 1 (T:p4-b6), which lists candidates with P_bound < 0.5 discovered by the Hypervelocity Star Survey. No individual astrometric, kinematic, distance, velocity, or bound-probability values are reported for HVS16 anywhere in the text, tables, captions, or figures; figures 1-5 show candidates only as unlabeled scatter points. Because the paper reports no star-specific quantity for HVS16, no values are extracted.

HVS17: HVS17 is not individually reported in the supplied text or images. Table 1 (T:p4-b6, I:p4-b6) includes it only within the grouped Hypervelocity Star Survey entry “HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others” and states that the table lists candidates with P_bound < 0.5; this is a selection threshold, not an individual measured value. The figures do not label HVS17, so no star-specific quantities can be extracted.

HVS18: The paper does not report individual astrometric or kinematic values (right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, or Galactic rest-frame velocity) for HVS18. It only includes HVS18 in the list of hypervelocity candidates with P_bound < 0.5 after Gaia DR2 (Table 1), so only that upper limit is recorded.

HVS19: HVS19 is not discussed individually anywhere in the supplied text; no position, parallax, distance, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius or total Galactic rest-frame speed is reported for it. The only star-specific statement is its membership in the Hypervelocity Star Survey group of Table 1, whose stars all have P_bound < 0.5 after Gaia DR2; the row lists names only as 'HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others', so HVS19 is included via the '12-24' range but the list is explicitly incomplete. Because Table 1 gives only this threshold for the group (no individual value), only the bound-probability upper limit is recorded; the associated unbound probability (>0.5) is not explicitly reported as a number. Table 1 additionally states these objects are predominantly early-type (38 B/A dwarfs plus one subdwarf O, one F9 dwarf and one white dwarf), consistent with HVS19 being a B/A star.

HVS20: HVS20 is identified only as part of the Hypervelocity Star Survey entry in Table 1. The paper does not provide individual astrometry, distance, radial velocity, or a numerical P_bound value for HVS20; Table 1 establishes only that it satisfies P_bound < 0.5 after Gaia DR2. I therefore record that threshold as an exclusive upper bound rather than as a measured point value.

HVS21: The paper only names HVS21 within the grouped Hypervelocity Star Survey entry (“HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others”) in Table 1 at T:p4-b6. It provides no individual astrometric, distance, velocity, or bound-probability measurement for HVS21, so no quantities are extracted for this target.

HVS22: HVS22 is not individually tabulated in the supplied material. Its only HVS22-specific information is inclusion in the Table 1 group of candidates with P_bound < 0.5, via the Hypervelocity Star Survey row naming HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others (T:p4-b6). No individual coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, or numerical probability for HVS22 is reported in the supplied text or figures.

HVS23: HVS23 is only identified as part of the Hypervelocity Star Survey entries in Table 1, whose names are listed as 'HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others' (T:p4-b6). The table's P_bound < 0.5 criterion is a selection threshold, not an individual reported measurement, so no star-specific quantity can be extracted for HVS23 from the supplied material.

HVS24: HVS24 is mentioned only in Table 1 at T:p4-b6, where it falls within the entry "HVS1,4-10,12-24 and others" for the Hypervelocity Star Survey (32 stars). Table 1 lists candidates with P_bound < 0.5, but this is a selection threshold, not a per-star measured result, and no individual astrometric, kinematic, distance, or probability values for HVS24 are reported in the supplied material. Therefore no quantities meeting the scientific rules can be extracted for this star.

US708: US708 is discussed only qualitatively as a helium subdwarf O star and likely supernova Ia donor/survivor. The supplied text reports no individual right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or exact bound/unbound probability for US708. Its placement in Table 1 implies only P_bound < 0.5; the exact value is not given, and unlabeled figure points cannot be uniquely assigned to it.

HE 0437-5439: The target HE 0437-5439 (HVS3) appears only as a named entry in Table 1 (T:p4-b6) and in a narrative sentence (T:p4-b8): "The star located beside the LMC is HVS3: an 8 M⊙ star thought to have been ejected from the LMC (Edelmann et al. 2005; Gualandris & Portegies Zwart 2007; Erkal et al. 2018)." The paper gives no position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius or rest-frame speed for this star. Its inclusion in Table 1 reflects only the selection criterion P_bound < 0.5, which under the rules is a selection threshold/sample membership rather than an individual reported result, so no bound-probability value is recorded. Figure 5 (I:p5-b1) shows its sky location but reports no numeric quantity.

HD 271791: Only a heliocentric distance is reported for HD 271791. Table 1 lists HD 271791 as a candidate from Heber et al. (2008) with P_bound < 0.5, but no individual RA, Dec, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactic rest-frame speed, galactocentric radius, or exact bound probability is given for this star.

SDSS J013655.91+242546.0: The target SDSS J013655.91+242546.0 appears only in Table 1 (T:p4-b6) as one of the Tillich et al. (2009) hypervelocity candidates with P_bound < 0.5. The paper gives no individual astrometric, kinematic, distance, or probability measurement for this star; the P_bound < 0.5 entry is a selection threshold, not an individual reported value.

LAMOST-HVS1: The target identifier LAMOST-HVS1 appears only as part of the "LAMOST HVS Survey" entry in Table 1 (T:p4-b6), which lists the three LAMOST-HVS1-3 stars collectively as candidates with P_bound < 0.5. The paper reports no individual position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for LAMOST-HVS1. The table count ("3") is a sample statistic for a group, not an individual result, so no quantities are extracted. (The late-type object discussed extensively, LAMOST J115209.12+120258.0 / Li10, is a different star from the target and its values are not attributed to LAMOST-HVS1.)

LAMOST-HVS2: The identifier "LAMOST-HVS2" appears in the paper only as part of the grouped entry "LAMOST-HVS1-3" in Table 1 (T:p4-b6: "LAMOST HVS Survey | 3 | LAMOST-HVS1-3"). The paper reports no individual measurements (position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, velocities, or bound probabilities) for LAMOST-HVS2 itself; only group-level sample statistics are given (e.g., T:p4-b3, T:p4-b6), which per the rules are not assigned as individual results. The only late-type object analyzed individually is LAMOST J115209.12+120258.0 (Li10; T:p5-b6, T:p5-b8), which is a distinct star from the early-type LAMOST-HVS1-3 and is not the target here. Note also that "HVS2" in Table 1 refers to US708, not LAMOST-HVS2. Therefore no eligible quantities are reported for the target star.

LAMOST-HVS3: The target star LAMOST-HVS3 appears only in Table 1 (T:p4-b6), where it is listed among the LAMOST HVS Survey (Zheng et al. 2014; Huang et al. 2017) candidates as "LAMOST-HVS1-3". The paper provides no individual numerical values (position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability) for LAMOST-HVS3 itself; only the aggregate list of candidates with P_bound < 0.5 is given, and selection thresholds/sample statistics are not individual results. No per-star quantities can be extracted.

Li10: The right ascension and declination are parsed from the reported LAMOST designation LAMOST J115209.12+120258.0; the paper does not list separate coordinate values. The only numerical bound probability is the pre-Gaia DR2 Li et al. (2015) value. After Gaia DR2, Li10 is placed in the P_bound < 0.5 subsample in Table 1 / Section 3.3, but that is a selection threshold rather than an exact individual probability, so no new exact bound probability is recorded.

GD 492: GD 492 is listed in Table 1 (T:p4-b6) among hypervelocity candidates with P_bound < 0.5, but that is a sample selection threshold applied to the table, not an individually reported bound-probability measurement; therefore no bound_probability value is recorded. No individual RA, Dec, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, or Galactic rest-frame velocity is reported for GD 492 in the supplied text.

SDSSJ124043.01+671034.68: The only supplied mention of SDSSJ124043.01+671034.68 is at T:p4-b11, which states that this white-dwarf hypervelocity candidate is confirmed with Gaia DR2 to be bound to the Galaxy. The paper reports no numerical values for the requested quantities for this star, so no quantities are retained.

Li2: Li2 (the second candidate of Li et al. 2015) is explicitly excluded from the analysis in T:p2-b9: the paper states "We also do not consider Li2 ... because there are two radial velocity measurements in the literature which disagree", suggesting it is likely an unresolved binary whose reported radial velocities do not reflect the systemic velocity. The only reported numbers for this star are the two conflicting radial velocities, which are recorded here as literature values; no astrometry, distance, parallax, proper motions, bound probability, Galactocentric radius or rest-frame speed are reported for Li2. Both radial velocity values are retained rather than a single adopted value, in line with the instruction not to choose a best value; note that they are ambiguous/irreconcilable per the authors.
